categories.name: Caller objective
categories.gloss: Caller says what they want or why they called
categories.speaker: CALLER

subcategories.name: Check stock / availability
subcategories.gloss: Asks if an item is in stock
subcategories.description: Caller asks whether a specific item, size or color is currently available in store or online.
examples: do you have this in stock

fields.name: Item description
fields.description: Product name or description the caller is asking about.

fields.name: Size
fields.description: Size requested, letter or numeric.

fields.name: Color
fields.description: Color or variant requested.

fields.name: Quantity in stock
fields.description: Units available as reported by the agent.

subcategories.name: Return / refund / exchange
subcategories.gloss: Asks about a return or refund
subcategories.description: Caller asks about, or requests, returning, exchanging or refunding an item, whether they already have it or are asking before buying.
examples: I'd like to return this item

fields.name: Return reason
fields.description: Stated reason for the return.

fields.name: Return window (days)
fields.description: Days allowed for return under the policy the agent quoted.

fields.name: Refund amount
fields.description: Amount to be refunded or credited.

fields.name: Order or receipt number
fields.description: Merchant order or receipt number used to look up the purchase.

subcategories.name: Shipping / delivery question
subcategories.gloss: Asks about shipping cost or timing
subcategories.description: Caller asks about shipping methods, cost or delivery timing.
examples: how much is delivery

fields.name: Shipping method
fields.description: Shipping tier discussed or chosen.

fields.name: Shipping cost
fields.description: Fee for the chosen shipping method.

fields.name: Delivery window
fields.description: Estimated delivery time frame or date range.

subcategories.name: Price, discount or promo question
subcategories.gloss: Asks about a discount or promo code
subcategories.description: Caller asks about discounts, promotions, promo codes or price matching.
examples: can I use a discount code

fields.name: Discount code
fields.description: Promo code applied to the order.

fields.name: Discount size
fields.description: Size of the discount granted, percent or amount.

fields.name: Price match requested
fields.description: Whether the caller asked for a price match against a competitor.

subcategories.name: Place order over the phone
subcategories.gloss: Wants to place an order by phone
subcategories.description: Caller wants to place or finish a purchase during the call.
examples: can I pay by card over the phone

fields.name: Payment method
fields.description: How the caller pays.

fields.name: Order total
fields.description: Final charged total for the order.

subcategories.name: In-store pickup / reservation
subcategories.gloss: Wants an item held for pickup
subcategories.description: Caller wants an item held, reserved or set up for click-and-collect or in-store pickup.
examples: can you hold that for me

fields.name: Store location
fields.description: Store or branch where the item is to be picked up.

fields.name: Hold duration
fields.description: How long the reservation or hold is valid for.

subcategories.name: Sizing / fit question
subcategories.gloss: Asks how an item fits or runs
subcategories.description: Caller asks how an item fits, runs, or which size to pick.
examples: does this run small or large

fields.name: Fit type
fields.description: How the item is described to fit.

subcategories.name: Restock / release date question
subcategories.description: Caller asks when an out-of-stock or upcoming item will become available.
examples: when will this be back in stock

fields.name: Restock ETA
fields.description: Expected restock or release date.

subcategories.name: Loyalty / rewards points question
subcategories.description: Caller asks about earning, checking or redeeming loyalty or rewards points.
examples: can I use my rewards points

fields.name: Points redeemed value
fields.description: Dollar value of points applied to the purchase.

categories.name: Reported issue
categories.gloss: Caller describes the problem, fee or dispute
categories.speaker: CALLER

subcategories.name: Wrong size / item received
subcategories.gloss: Received the wrong size or item
subcategories.description: Caller states they received the wrong size, color or item versus what was ordered.
examples: I ordered a medium but got a large

fields.name: Expected value
fields.description: What the caller ordered.

fields.name: Received value
fields.description: What actually arrived.

subcategories.name: Item doesn't fit
subcategories.description: Caller states a purchased item doesn't fit as expected, independent of a shipping error.
examples: it doesn't fit me properly

fields.name: Fit problem
fields.description: Nature of the fit problem.

subcategories.name: Item quality / condition defect
subcategories.description: Caller reports the item arrived damaged, worn or of lower quality than expected.
examples: it looked used when it arrived

subcategories.name: Billing / charge dispute
subcategories.description: Caller disputes a charge, fee, or a refusal to refund.
examples: I was charged a fee I don't agree with

fields.name: Disputed amount
fields.description: Amount in dispute.

subcategories.name: Lost / undelivered parcel
subcategories.description: Caller reports an expected delivery never arrived.
examples: my parcel never showed up

subcategories.name: Suspicious email / possible scam
subcategories.description: Caller reports a promotional email or code that may be fraudulent.
examples: this email looks like a scam

categories.name: Friction point
categories.gloss: Caller describes an obstacle, repeat failure or frustration
categories.speaker: CALLER

subcategories.name: Can't identify the correct product
subcategories.description: Caller and agent struggle over several turns to pin down exactly which product or stock number is meant.
examples: I'm not sure which item that is

subcategories.name: Call quality / connection trouble
subcategories.description: Caller or agent notes the line is breaking up or one side can't hear the other.
examples: can you hear me, the line is breaking up

subcategories.name: No printer for return label
subcategories.gloss: Has no printer for a return label
subcategories.description: Caller states they lack a printer needed to complete a return.
examples: I don't have a printer at home

subcategories.name: Agent perceived as rude/dismissive
subcategories.gloss: Finds the agent rude or dismissive
subcategories.description: Caller states the agent is being rude, dismissive or condescending.
examples: you're being quite rude

subcategories.name: Past bad experience at another retailer
subcategories.description: Caller references frustration from a previous purchase or return experience elsewhere.
examples: another store gave me trouble before

subcategories.name: Extensive prior search / effort
subcategories.description: Caller describes having already spent significant time or effort trying to find the item.
examples: I've been looking everywhere for this

categories.name: Proposed fix
categories.gloss: Agent proposes a fix or workaround
categories.speaker: AGENT

subcategories.name: Offer replacement item
subcategories.description: Agent offers to send a replacement in the correct size, color or condition.
examples: we can send a replacement

subcategories.name: Offer refund / store credit
subcategories.gloss: Offers a refund or store credit
subcategories.description: Agent offers a refund, rebate or store credit as the resolution.
examples: we can process a refund for you

subcategories.name: Offer alternate store / special order
subcategories.description: Agent offers to source the item from another location, ship it specially, or special-order it.
examples: we can order that from another store

subcategories.name: Offer discount / courtesy credit
subcategories.description: Agent offers a discount, voucher or goodwill credit for the caller's trouble.
examples: we can offer you a discount for the trouble

subcategories.name: Offer hold / reservation
subcategories.description: Agent offers to hold or reserve stock or tickets for a limited time.
examples: we can hold that for you

subcategories.name: Offer price match
subcategories.description: Agent agrees to try to match a competitor's price.
examples: we can try to match that price

phrases: \b(we|i)('ll| will| can| could| would| shall| am going to|'m going to|'m gonna| am gonna)( \w+){0,3} (send|process|refund|credit|exchange|replace|reserve|hold|order|match|discount|waive|offer|ship|transfer|arrange|put|do|issue|get|source|call|try)\b

categories.name: Agent completed
categories.gloss: Agent reports that an action is done
categories.speaker: AGENT

subcategories.name: Order / payment confirmed
subcategories.description: Agent reports the order was placed or payment processed successfully.
examples: your payment has gone through

subcategories.name: Return / refund initiated
subcategories.description: Agent reports the return, label or refund process has been started or completed on their end.
examples: I've started the refund on our end

subcategories.name: Reservation / hold placed
subcategories.description: Agent reports an item has been reserved, held or added to the caller's account.
examples: that's reserved under your name

subcategories.name: Account / loyalty record updated
subcategories.description: Agent reports account, membership or loyalty details were created or updated.
examples: I've added that to your account

categories.name: Caller confirmed
categories.gloss: Caller confirms the problem is solved
categories.speaker: CALLER

subcategories.name: Satisfied with answer / purchase
subcategories.description: Caller expresses satisfaction and closes out the call positively.
examples: that's all, thank you so much

subcategories.name: Explicit confirmation of details
subcategories.description: Caller explicitly confirms a specific detail, quote or plan is correct or acceptable.
examples: yes, that all sounds good

phrases: \b(that'?s|that is|sounds|it'?s|that would be|that'?d be|that will be|that'?ll be) (perfect|great|good|brilliant|fine|awesome|correct|lovely|wonderful|excellent|helpful|amazing)\b

subcategories.name: Dispute not accepted by caller
subcategories.description: Caller explicitly rejects the agent's position and states the matter is not settled.
examples: I'll take this further, that's not right

categories.name: Deferred
categories.gloss: Agent defers work or promises a callback
categories.speaker: AGENT

subcategories.name: Follow-up notification promised
subcategories.description: Agent promises a confirmation email, text or tracking update will follow later.
examples: you'll get a confirmation email shortly

subcategories.name: Pending supplier restock / special order
subcategories.description: Agent defers fulfillment because the item must come from a supplier or another location first.
examples: that's on order from our supplier

subcategories.name: Escalate to colleague / manager
subcategories.description: Agent brings in, or refers to, another staff member for part of the request.
examples: let me just get my manager

phrases: \b(i|we|they)('ll| will) (send|email|notify|let you know|call|contact|text|reach out|be in touch)\b

categories.name: Upsell / cross-sell attempt
categories.description: Agent proactively offers an add-on item, membership, retention deal, or spending nudge beyond what the caller asked for.
categories.speaker: AGENT

subcategories.name: Add-on / accessory cross-sell
subcategories.description: Agent offers a related add-on item, such as gift wrap, a case or a bundle, not requested by the caller.
examples: would you like to add a case with that

fields.name: Add-on item
fields.description: The add-on item offered.

fields.name: Add-on price
fields.description: Price of the add-on.

subcategories.name: Loyalty / membership enrollment pitch
subcategories.description: Agent invites the caller to join a loyalty, rewards or VIP program.
examples: would you like to join our rewards program

fields.name: Program name
fields.description: Name of the loyalty or membership program pitched.

subcategories.name: Retention discount offer (cancel-save)
subcategories.description: Agent offers a discounted continuation when the caller is trying to cancel.
examples: we could offer a discounted rate instead

fields.name: Retention offer price
fields.description: Discounted price offered to retain the customer.

subcategories.name: Free-shipping threshold nudge
subcategories.description: Agent suggests adding items to reach a free-shipping spending threshold.
examples: a bit more would qualify you for free shipping

categories.name: Agent conduct concern
categories.description: Agent's tone or remarks depart from a professional register: over-familiar sales talk, jokes about sensitive data, or dismissiveness toward the caller. Experimental: seeded from 3 of 30 calls; monitor as more calls are scored.
categories.speaker: AGENT

subcategories.name: Overly familiar / self-promotional pitch
subcategories.description: Agent brags about personal sales performance or makes personal remarks that overstep a professional register.
examples: I'm actually the top rep in the store

subcategories.name: Joke about sensitive data collection
subcategories.description: Agent jokes while asking for account or payment details in a way that trivializes sensitive-data handling.
examples: and your social security number, just kidding

subcategories.name: Dismissive or skeptical tone
subcategories.description: Agent's tone reads as dismissive of, or skeptical toward, what the caller is telling them.
examples: that seems unlikely, doesn't it

notes: Retail seed derived from 30 AppTek retail ground-truth transcripts (sample_audio/apptek_retail), read in full, text only. Adds retail subcategories to the 8 built-in categories and two custom categories (upsell_attempt, agent_conduct_concern). competitor_mention was evaluated and excluded for thin support (2/30 calls). All PII-forbidden extraction fields (card number, CVV, customer name, email, phone, mailing address, loyalty/account number) were dropped rather than seeded, per contract 1.3.0 section 5.2.
